_comment: How to give one task to each coding agent without a branch per agent in the driver.
Every invocation here was verified by running it: the four agents in this cluster have four
different non-interactive front doors and one of them refuses to run at all without an explicit
session id. That is the whole reason this file exists as data -- the differences are facts about
someone else's CLI, and encoding them as code would put four `if agent ==` branches in the middle
`argv` is a template. `{prompt}` is the task text and `{session}` is a per-run identifier the
driver generates. A fresh session per run is not hygiene, it is the experiment: hermes was
observed sending 258 input tokens on one call and 15,510 on the next because the second inherited
the first, so a run that reuses a session measures the previous run as well.
`workspace` is where the agent is started. Each run gets its own directory so one agent's leftover
files cannot become another agent's context.
NOT recorded here: which model to use. The model is the Service alias's business, and an agent that
names a model in its own invocation would let the driver silently break the one thing this

opencode.notes: Reports the model it resolved on stderr, which is worth capturing as a check that the alias took effect.

qwen-code.notes: A positional query is also one-shot; -p is the documented non-interactive flag.

hermes.notes: -z is the non-interactive prompt. Its config is pod-local state (hermes config set), not a ConfigMap, so a pod replacement resets the model and the driver re-checks it.

openclaw.notes: Refuses to run without --session-id, --to or --agent. Tries the Gateway first and falls back to an embedded agent; both paths reach the alias.
